candidate_relations.reason: CD68-positive dermal histiocytes establish histiocytosis, but neither generalized eruptive subtype nor clonal leukemia is specified.
Biopsy lacked lipid-laden foam cells, giant cells, and necrobiosis expected in necrobiotic xanthogranuloma.
Eosinophils of 4220/μL and marrow eosinophilia fit hypereosinophilia, but the FIP1L1-PDGFRA clone and GEH require greater specificity.
The infiltrate was CD1a negative, whereas indeterminate-cell histiocytosis generally retains CD1a expression.
No long-bone, perirenal, cardiovascular, or CNS lesions appeared on systemic imaging.
Marrow myeloid hyperplasia and fusion-positive eosinophilia support an eosinophilic MPN but omit the associated GEH.
Skin biopsy showed histiocytes rather than epidermotropic atypical T cells.
The FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion and marrow eosinophilia identify the leukemia, but the generalized eruptive histiocytosis component is absent.
Dermal cells expressed CD68 and stabilin-1 as GEH, with no demonstration that they were eosinophilic leukemic blasts.
Dermal eosinophils accompanied the papules, but histiocytes formed the nodules and systemic leukemia was fusion-defined.
Marked blood and marrow eosinophilia fits an eosinophilic disorder but leaves both clonality and GEH unspecified.
